t.1.187.1: Then the greatly splendid Pāñcāla king summoned the prince Yudhiṣṭhira and received him with the welcome due to a brahmin.
t.1.187.2: The undaunted one questioned the radiant son of Kuntī: "How are we to know you, as kṣatriyas or as brāhmaṇas?"
t.1.187.3: Or are you vaiśyas endowed with virtues, or men born of śūdra wombs, or siddhas who have assumed a magical disguise and wander in every direction?
t.1.187.4: Or are you beings who have come down from heaven for Kṛṣṇā's sake, wishing to see her? Let your honour tell us the truth, for great is our doubt in this matter.
t.1.187.5: At the end of our doubt, may contentment now enter our mind here? May our portions of fortune prove auspicious, O scorcher of foes?
t.1.187.7: For having heard your words, O you who are like an immortal, O tamer of foes, I shall surely undertake the performance of the marriage in accordance with the prescribed rites.
t.1.187.6: Please, tell me the truth, for truth shines among kings, just as it does together with sacrifices and pious works; a falsehood must never be spoken.
t.1.187.8: Do not be downcast, O king; O Pāñcālya, let there be joy for you. This cherished wish of yours has surely come true, without a doubt.
t.1.187.10: And the twins are there, O king of kings, where Kṛṣṇā is settled. Let the sorrow of your mind depart; we are kṣatriyas, O bull among men. This daughter of yours has gone like a lotus-plant from one lake to another lake.
t.1.187.9: We are indeed kṣatriyas, O king, the sons of the great-souled Pāṇḍu. Know me to be the eldest, the son of Kuntī, and these two to be Bhīmasena and Arjuna, by whom your daughter was won, O king, in the assembly of kings.
t.1.187.11: Thus, great king, I tell you all this truthfully, for you are our guru and our highest refuge.
t.1.187.12: Then King Drupada, his eyes overwhelmed with joy, was unable at that moment to make a fitting reply to Yudhiṣṭhira.
t.1.187.13: But the king, scorcher of foes, having restrained that joy with effort, then replied to Yudhiṣṭhira in fitting words.
t.1.187.15: Having heard that speech of the son of Kuntī, King Drupada then censured Dhṛtarāṣṭra, the lord of men.
t.1.187.14: And the righteous-souled one asked him how they had fled in the past, and the Pāṇḍava told him everything in due order.
t.1.187.16: And Drupada, best of speakers, comforted that son of Kuntī, Yudhiṣṭhira, and pledged himself to the cause of his kingdom.
t.1.187.18: There they dwelt, O king, honored by Yajñasena. Then, when they had recovered their ease, the king, together with his sons, spoke to them.
t.1.187.17: Then Kuntī and Kṛṣṇā, Bhīmasena and Arjuna as well, and the twins, directed by the king, entered the great palace.
t.1.187.19: Let the joy of the Kurus take her hand according to the rite this very day; on this auspicious day let the mighty-armed Arjuna hold the festive ceremony.
t.1.187.21: Let your honor take the hand of my daughter according to the rite, or else, O hero, assign Kṛṣṇā to whomever you think fit.
t.1.187.20: Then King Yudhiṣṭhira, the son of Dharma, said to him: “O lord of the people, a marriage must first be made for me as well.”
t.1.187.22: O king, Draupadī shall be the queen of us all, for thus it was spoken before by my mother, O lord of the people.
t.1.187.23: I too am still unmarried, and so is Bhīmasena the Pāṇḍava; this daughter of yours, a very jewel among women, has been won by Pārtha.
t.1.187.24: This, O king, is our agreement: the shared enjoyment of a jewel. And we do not wish to abandon that agreement, O best of kings.
t.1.187.25: Kṛṣṇā shall lawfully be the chief queen of all of us; let her take the hand of each of us in turn before the fire.
t.1.187.26: For one man many queens have been ordained, O joy of the Kurus, but many men are never ordained for one woman.
t.1.187.28: Subtle is dharma, great king; we do not know its course. We follow the path trodden by our forebears, one after another in due succession.
t.1.187.27: You are righteous and pure, O Kaunteya, and ought not to commit an unrighteous act that is opposed to both the world and the Veda. Why is your mind set on such a thing?
t.1.187.29: My speech has never uttered a falsehood, nor is my mind set upon adharma. Thus indeed my mother speaks, and thus indeed is the thought within my mind.
t.1.187.30: This is the eternal dharma, O king; practise it without hesitation. And let there be no misgiving in you about this in any way, O lord of the earth.
t.1.187.32: Then, having come together, they all conversed, O Bhārata; and then, O king, Dvaipāyana arrived there by chance.
t.1.187.31: You, O son of Kuntī, and Kuntī, and my son Dhṛṣṭadyumna: let them declare what is to be done, and tomorrow, at the proper time, we shall do it.
